prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of a whole small white harbour town on an island in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE WHITE TOWN OF BIBLIA, THE TOWN OF THE RECORDS, ON AN ISLAND IN A CALM INNER SEA: a small harbour town where everything is white: white stone houses, white flagstone streets, a low white sea wall around the town. At the top middle the colossal WHITE ARCHIVE, a vast library of white marble with a dome, behind a low inner wall with an open gate; to its left the long Hall of the Records with a portico, to its right the great library with a pale green copper roof. In the middle a paved plaza with a round fountain and the white statue of a hooded girl storyteller holding an open book. Noa's inn on the left, the tavern on the right, a shop with a striped awning and small white houses in the south, a white stone quay along the sea with a wooden pier and a white two-masted ship moored beside it. Small lawns with white and pale blue flowers, a few slender pale trees. Palette: whites, ivory, pale greys, very pale blue-greys, soft greens, dark sea blue. Quiet, faded, as if the town were slowly turning into a blank page.

The WHITE ARCHIVE is the key landmark: the biggest building, filling the top middle, all white stone with a great arched door in the middle of its south front. Every building is white or off-white stone; roofs are pale grey slate, white tiles or pale green copper (NO dark blue roofs). The wooden pier and the white ship moored beside it are in the sea at the bottom. A few loose white paper sheets lie scattered on the streets here and there, as if blown by the wind.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 56 x 46 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2688 x 2208 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, hue-shifted ramps, level of detail), but use the palette of THE PLACE below. Do NOT copy anything from it (no buildings, piers, water or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, meadows, rocks and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- green = short LAWN grass of small gardens (walkable, flat), green with small dots = little white and pale blue FLOWERS in the grass (walkable).
- light grey with block lines = pale WHITE FLAGSTONE streets and plazas (walkable, flat).
- brown with plank lines = a wooden PIER of dark planks on posts (walkable).
- dark blue with small arcs = the calm night SEA of the inner sea (not walkable).
- blue = the dark water of a fountain basin (not walkable).
- dark green circles = single slender pale-barked TREES with small round crowns (not walkable).
- off-white blocks = WHITE BUILDINGS and WHITE STONE WALLS (not walkable), as the landmarks describe: roofs of pale grey slate, white stone tiles or pale green copper, their south faces with windows and doors.
All colour areas are LEVEL GROUND unless listed as not walkable.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(236,234,228) = a low wall of WHITE STONE around the town, its top edge seen from above (the sea is beyond it).
- the blocks in colour rgb(222,220,212) = a low WHITE STONE WALL with a coping on top, dividing the north district from the town.
- the blocks in colour rgb(214,212,204) = an open arched GATE passage through the white wall (walkable), two white pillars at its sides.
- the blocks in colour rgb(130,92,58) = a wooden PIER of dark planks on posts, reaching out into the sea (walkable).
- the blocks in colour rgb(232,230,222) = a white-hulled two-masted sailing SHIP moored alongside the pier (seen from above: long pale deck, two masts with furled white sails, a small cabin at the stern).
- the blocks in colour rgb(110,140,180) = a round white marble FOUNTAIN basin of dark water; in its middle a white stone STATUE of a hooded girl storyteller in a long cloak holding an open book, on a round pedestal.
- the blocks in colour rgb(240,238,232) = the WHITE ARCHIVE: a colossal library of white marble seen from above, a great pale roof of white stone tiles with a round dome and many small skylights, tall buttresses, a grand arched great DOOR in the middle of its south front.
- small BLACK rectangles = the front DOORS / openings. Paint each door exactly at that spot and size (a wooden door or a dark opening, its bottom edge on the bottom edge of the wall). Do not add any other door or opening that looks like a door.
- the blocks in colour rgb(168,172,184) = the HALL OF THE RECORDS: a long white stone hall with a pale grey slate roof, a row of tall windows and a portico of slim columns.
- the blocks in colour rgb(150,186,170) = the GREAT LIBRARY: a tall white building with a pale green copper roof and a small bell turret.
- the blocks in colour rgb(176,184,200) = NOA'S INN: a two-storey white house with a pale blue-grey roof, a wooden balcony and a hanging sign bracket.
- the blocks in colour rgb(178,174,170) = the TAVERN: a white house with a round window and a pale grey roof, barrels by the wall.
- the blocks in colour rgb(172,176,186) = a narrow white townhouse with a grey roof.
- the blocks in colour rgb(172,176,186) = a narrow white townhouse with a grey roof.
- the blocks in colour rgb(190,172,156) = the SHOP: a white stone shop with a striped awning over its front.
- the blocks in colour rgb(172,176,186) = a white house with a grey roof and window boxes.
- the blocks in colour rgb(172,176,186) = a white house with a grey roof and window boxes.
- the blocks in colour rgb(172,176,186) = a white house with a grey roof.
- the blocks in colour rgb(96,66,44) = a wooden NOTICE BOARD on two posts covered with many pinned papers.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, boats or ships on the water (unless a landmark says so), treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
